evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: Key terms like "content identification" and "fingerprinting" are not specified (audio fingerprinting vs other media/content), allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: "Profile" is underspecified (listening history, demographics, preferences, explicit settings), leading to different requirement interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: "Similar" is undefined (behavioral similarity, demographics, taste vectors), enabling materially different matching approaches.

evaluations.evidence: music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: "Similar" and "content similarity" are unclear (audio similarity, visual similarity, metadata similarity), yielding different functional requirements.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags ... related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: Terms like "enriched metadata", "image tags", and "relevant listening path" are vague and can be interpreted in multiple materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: "Tags" (format, schema, source) and "all further processing steps" are undefined, allowing different interpretations of scope and propagation.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what constitutes a "thumbnail sequence" (sampling rate, ordering, length) and what defines "video segments" (shots, scenes, fixed intervals).

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: "Info" and "similar" are underspecified, leading to different outputs (metadata vs previews vs similarity scores) and similarity definitions.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: "Perceptually similar" is unclear (visual-only, audio-only, multimodal; which perceptual model), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: "Content" and "similar profiles" are not defined, allowing different recommendation targets and similarity criteria.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: "Most relevant" and "my area" are vague (radius, administrative boundary, current location vs home), leading to different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: "Identify" could mean detect faces, recognize known individuals, or track persons; "related information" is also unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: "Identify products" could mean detect product categories, specific SKUs/brands, or logos; "related information" is undefined.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: While "broadcaster logos" is clearer, "identify" (detect vs recognize which broadcaster) and "related information" remain underspecified.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: "Identify brands" could mean logo detection, text recognition, or product inference; "related information" is ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: "Related" is undefined (visual similarity, same subject, same location/event), producing materially different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: walk around, access content using a geographical map and be informed if there are videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: "Covering the area" and "relevant point of interest" are vague; notification conditions and geographic scope can vary materially.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what "content items" are (videos only vs audio too) and how ASR is used (search transcripts, keywords, speaker).

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: "Segmentation" is underspecified (shots/scenes/chapters; algorithmic vs manual), leading to different editing/validation requirements.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: "Annotate" and "topic" are not defined (taxonomy vs free text; single vs multiple topics), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: "A/V quality aspects" is vague (resolution, bitrate, loudness, artifacts, etc.), allowing materially different ranking criteria.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: "Edited" is ambiguous (cut/trim, noise reduction, compression, remixing) and "quick assessment" lacks a defined threshold/behavior.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: "Nudity content" and what counts as "prefilter" (block, flag, blur; thresholds) are open to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: "Prefilter", "content", and "low-level asset information" are underspecified, enabling different functional meanings and data fields.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what "validated" entails (detect, flag, block) and what "copyright infringement" detection method/criteria apply.

evaluations.evidence: high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: "High-level asset information" and "recognized" vs "provided" tags are unclear in scope and meaning; "prefilter" behavior is also ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is
evaluations.rationale: Subjective terms "interesting", "appealing", and "complex" lack operational definition, allowing materially different scoring/criteria.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject
evaluations.rationale: "Should be prompted" and what constitutes a trigger condition are undefined; "subject" could also vary by project context.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: "Volunteer types" is undefined (skill level, engagement segments, demographics, roles), leading to different classification schemes.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: "Preclassify" and "simple low-level image features" are vague (which features; what classes), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: images with no classifiable animals in them
evaluations.rationale: "Classifiable animals" is ambiguous (no animals vs animals too small/blurred/occluded), affecting detection criteria materially.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: "Image series detection" and what constitutes a "timestamping malfunction" are underspecified, allowing different detection logic.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification
evaluations.rationale: "Preclassification" is unclear (coarse grouping vs full species label; confidence thresholds), enabling multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification
evaluations.rationale: "Attribute" is undefined (age, sex, behavior, markings, etc.), leading to materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether this means counting individuals, estimating ranges, or detecting presence/absence; counting rules are unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton
evaluations.rationale: Uses an "or" between two different functions (segmentation vs localization) without clarifying which is required, creating multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: images with no classifiable plankton in them
evaluations.rationale: "Classifiable plankton" is ambiguous (none present vs present but unidentifiable), affecting filtering criteria.

evaluations.evidence: detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether size, orientation, or both are required; also unclear how size is measured (pixels vs real units) and orientation definition.

evaluations.evidence: automatic preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: "Preclassification" is underspecified (taxonomy level, confidence thresholds, output format), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: "Reduce video duration" is ambiguous (trim idle segments, speed-up playback, summarize), leading to different functional outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: "The time" could mean timestamp of first frame, interval, or event window; egg-laying definition/criteria are not specified.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc
evaluations.rationale: "Important features" is vague and the list is non-exhaustive ("etc"), allowing materially different feature sets and priorities.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: "Probability/weight" and "experience" are undefined (tenure, accuracy, volume), enabling different scoring models and meanings.

evaluations.evidence: remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: "Remove artefacts" is ambiguous (mask, delete images, correct pixels) and the artefact set is open-ended ("such as").

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects
evaluations.rationale: "Moving" and especially "transient" objects are not defined (timescale, thresholds), leading to different detection criteria.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds from the audio files
evaluations.rationale: "Background noise" and "distracting sounds" are subjective/underspecified (what counts; how much removal), enabling different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: "Similar" is undefined (frequency contour, duration, species, call type), allowing materially different grouping behavior.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether to estimate individuals vs simultaneous callers; "heard" could mean detected calls vs confirmed whales.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: "Interrupt" and the conditions for "should" are undefined (timing, triggers, purpose), enabling multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Still ambiguous what "interrupt" means and what decision criteria determine modality; multiple materially different rules could satisfy it.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: "Educate" and the trigger conditions for "should" are undefined, allowing different interpretations of interventions.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous criteria for choosing modality and what "educate" entails; could be tutorials, hints, feedback, etc.

evaluations.evidence: know which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: "Piece of education" is unclear (lesson, hint, article, message template) and selection criteria are unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: know when a volunteer has made an interesting comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: "Interesting comment" is subjective and undefined; "subject" may also be interpreted differently across projects.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: "Should comment" lacks defined triggers/criteria; "comment" content/purpose is unspecified, enabling multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: "Explanation" and the conditions for when it "should" be given are underspecified, allowing different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: know what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous scope and constraints of "what ... should say" (templates vs generated text; tone; context), enabling materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: "Similarity" is undefined (visual, metadata, annotation patterns), leading to different grouping outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: "Previous experiences" is vague (projects participated in, performance, interests, time spent), enabling different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: "Articles" and "summary" are underspecified (which articles; what summary format/length), and "reuse" is unclear (republish, reference, template).
